lesson_title: Why One Dead Bulb Doesn't Black Out Your House
hook_text: A bulb blows in your bedroom, but the fridge keeps humming and the TV stays on. Why doesn't everything go dark?
clip_script: A bulb blows in your bedroom. The fridge keeps humming. The TV stays on. That is because your house is wired in parallel. The current splits into separate branches, like a highway splitting into many lanes at a toll plaza. Each branch connects straight across the supply, so every appliance gets the full two hundred and thirty volts, and each one works on its own. Close one lane and the others keep moving. Here is the twist. Add another bulb in parallel and it shines just as brightly as the first. Adding paths makes it easier for charge to flow, so the total resistance goes down and the total current goes up, like opening more tills at a supermarket. That is also the danger: plug a kettle, a heater and a microwave into one multi-plug and the currents add up until the wires overheat.
visual_style: A whiteboard house cutaway with glowing branches to each appliance, one bulb going dark while others stay lit, then a highway splitting into lanes and a multi-plug glowing red.
mood: Reassuring, with a sharp safety twist.
pacing: A familiar moment, a clear analogy, then a quick warning.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and compare series with parallel.
